summary: Smoke regression after docker-compose / Caddyfile / INSTALL.bat overhaul (deployment-only artifacts). 50/50 backend tests GREEN — 15 new iter_5 smoke (every endpoint listed in review_request) + 17 iter_4 rebrand suite + 18 iter_3 clone-smoke suite. Confirmed: backend Python/runtime untouched; /health=ok with mongo_connected=true; admin login admin@realtraffic.local/admin123 → 200 is_admin=true; wrong-password → 4xx; all admin listing endpoints (users, stats, system-check, ua-versions) → 200 with admin token; /api/branding.app_name == 'RealTraffic'; RUT engine-status & jobs listing reachable; CPI mounted (/api/cpi/offers, /api/cpi/dashboard/stats not 404); sub-users + form-filler/jobs listing reachable; user register→login→/api/auth/me round-trip works; RUT POST concurrency=20 → 400 (cap mentions 15); RUT POST fast_mode=true accepted (200 with concurrency=15+fast_mode=true echoed back, job_id issued); old creds (admin@realflow.local) correctly 401. Zero 5xx anywhere. Total wall-time 8s.

minor.issue: (Pre-existing from iter_3/iter_4) route is on bare `app` not `api_router` so it is not reachable via public ingress (only internal localhost:8001/health). Move under /api or add ingress rule.

(Pre-existing from iter_4) Returns 401 'User not found' with admin token because admin is env-only (not in users coll) and CPI uses get_current_user_with_fresh_data. Endpoint is mounted (not 404) — works for registered+activated users. Auto-provision admin row on first admin login OR add admin guard on CPI routes.

action_items: (No regression — no required action) Deployment artifacts (docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile, INSTALL.bat) did not perturb backend behavior. Safe to ship.
(Optional, carried over) Move /health under /api or add ingress rule so external uptime probes work.

critical_code_review_comments: docker-compose.yml + Caddyfile + INSTALL.bat are deployment-only and correctly do NOT introduce any backend Python imports or runtime hooks — backend behavior is byte-identical to iter_4 (50/50 regression confirms).

INSTALL.bat generates random JWT_SECRET / admin password on first run and writes to backend/.env — this is the right pattern. Verify in deployment that the generated values are persisted and not regenerated on subsequent `docker compose up` (would invalidate user sessions).

Caddy auto-Let's-Encrypt requires port 80/443 reachable from public internet — ensure DDNS-updater service runs BEFORE Caddy attempts ACME challenge on first boot, or first-cert issuance will fail. Suggest adding `depends_on: ddns-updater` with healthcheck.
